comparator: At each frozen branch point, baseline is the unchanged run.py instructions and complete contextual 121-action mapping. frontier-v2 uses the frozen goal/action questions with the same complete contextual action mapping.
knownSemanticLimits: goal_refresh_reasons refreshes an active priority only when it conflicts with the selected goal; clearing a prompt, combat, hunger, or low-HP signal can leave that goal active until the six-action horizon

route search treats a previously traversed adjacent edge as historically traversable in reverse even when that reverse transition was not itself observed; reverse route directions are inferred historical facts, not current safety guarantees
frontier_context omits observedAt and lastTraversedAt ages from the question state, so Jev cannot distinguish old from recent graph facts
the prompt regex has narrow deterministic fixture coverage and may miss other NetHack prompts
conditionImpairment is exposed as a signal but does not independently refresh an active goal

goal_refresh_reasons checks each simultaneously true prompt, low-HP, combat, and hunger signal against a different goal; with compound signals no one goal can satisfy all checks, so the candidate may refresh on every action and fail to realize the six-action horizon
operationalRules: A fixed global ledger reserves and fsyncs one attempted call before every goal or action request.
Failed, timeout, malformed-response, cancelled, and crash-ambiguous reservations consume the 192-attempt cap.
The single-use release and single-writer lock permit one execution attempt only.

Any crash, cancellation, provider error, replay mismatch, or preservation error ends the entire trial incomplete with partial evidence retained; no rerun, replacement point, favorable-outcome rerun, or extension is permitted.
All 121 ordered action IDs and their frozen base-label/action-keycode digest are checked before every request; no action is masked, removed, reweighted, or overridden.
A terminal arm stops and is retained; it is never reset or replaced.
Every replay starts frontier memory empty at reset and updates it only from run.make_state over the current captured raw observation before each historical action.
Mid-run resume is unsupported; an interrupted execution is terminal incomplete because memory, active goal, NLE step, and provider reservation are not recovered as one atomic checkpoint.

primaryMetric.aggregate: sum the two frozen pair deltas
primaryMetric.armValue: count of distinct positions reached by the 32 future actions that were absent from that branch point's exact replay prefix

decision.incomplete: any arm lacks its terminal or full 32-action retained result
decision.negative: aggregate < 0 or any safety gate fails
decision.positive: aggregate > 0 and neither pairDelta < 0 and all safety gates pass

primaryMetric.name: new_positions_vs_exact_prefix

safetyGates.menu: fail if a visible prompt is followed by an action whose contextual label is not a current prompt, inventory, answer, escape, Enter, Space, or --More-- handler
safetyGates.priority: fail if a newly selected frontier-v2 goal conflicts with an observed visible-prompt, low-HP, combat, or urgent-hunger priority
safetyGates.replacementCycle: fail if frontier-v2 has at least 16 future actions and either one two-position reversal pattern covers at least half its movement actions or one three-action action-label pattern repeats at least four consecutive times
safetyGates.terminal: fail if frontier-v2 terminates without verified ascension where its paired baseline does not; an early terminal is retained and never replaced

scope: exploratory development evidence only; never a generalization, ascension, or live-migration claim
secondaryMetrics: depth, score, experience level, NetHack turn, HP and hunger deltas
two-step reversals and repeated observed-edge traversals
observed frontier targets reached and known-route-distance sequence
exact raw no-ops, unchanged-position actions, and blank-or-wall attempts
